paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: greatness in God's kingdom runs backwards. The disciples were arguing about which of them was the greatest, and Jesus sat down and said, "If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all." (Mark 9:35) Then He put a little child in the middle of the room and held that child in His arms. I think He was showing them that the ones who look small are the ones He lifts up.

That same upside-down thinking shows up when John wants to stop a man who was driving out demons in Jesus' name. Jesus tells him, "For whoever is not against us is for us." (Mark 9:40) And a cup of water given because you bear the name of Christ? "He will never lose his reward." (Mark 9:41) Nothing done for Him is too small to count, and nobody gets to run a club with a guest list that Jesus never wrote.

Then Jesus gets serious, and I think this part is heavy. Causing one of His little ones to stumble matters to Him (Mark 9:42), and so does sin in your own life. His words about the hand, the foot and the eye show how seriously He wants us to take it (Mark 9:43-47). So here's what I want you to take with you, baker: serve before you shine, welcome before you gatekeep, and have "salt among yourselves," and "be at peace with one another." (Mark 9:50)
